title: kbmon sessions panel: Claude Code sessions, worktrees with branches, dispatch runs, stalled items, orphans
goal: the sessions panel of kbmon.py shows each process working in a checkout of the clone with its pid, age, class (orphan, hook or foreign) and checkout relative to the clone from backlog.py's process inventory, each worktree with its branch, the stalled items with their signals from backlog.py stalled and no absolute path of the clone; each Claude Code process is marked headless with its item when its checkout is a worker worktree on a work/<id> branch and interactive otherwise; a host that cannot list working directories shows the panel as unsupported

clauses.clause: the sessions panel of kbmon.py shows each process working in a checkout of the clone with its pid, age, class (orphan, hook or foreign) and checkout relative to the clone from backlog.py's process inventory, each worktree with its branch, the stalled items with their signals from backlog.py stalled and no absolute path of the clone
each Claude Code process is marked headless with its item when its checkout is a worker worktree on a work/<id> branch and interactive otherwise
a host that cannot list working directories shows the panel as unsupported

gates.question: Which processes does the sessions panel count as Claude Code sessions?
options: a process whose command name is claude: headless in a worker worktree on work/<id>, else interactive
also each coord session/<id> presence lease
gates.recommendation: a process whose command name is claude: headless in a worker worktree on work/<id>, else interactive
gates.answer: a process whose command name is claude: headless in a worker worktree on work/<id>, else interactive

gates.question: Does the sessions panel read the forge for the mr-dead signal of backlog.py stalled?
options: no: the panel starts no network request, so mr-dead is never read
yes: one forge read for each claimed item
gates.recommendation: no: the panel starts no network request, so mr-dead is never read
gates.answer: no: the panel starts no network request, so mr-dead is never read

gates.question: How does the panel show a process's checkout and a worktree's path?
options: relative to the clone: . for the clone, the path under it, else the directory name
the directory name alone, as backlog.py procs prints it
gates.recommendation: relative to the clone: . for the clone, the path under it, else the directory name
gates.answer: relative to the clone: . for the clone, the path under it, else the directory name

gates.question: Which stalled items does the panel list, and what do other processes show as session?
options: only items with a signal; a process that is no claude one has null session and item
also items with only an unknown signal; a non-claude process shows session none
gates.recommendation: only items with a signal; a process that is no claude one has null session and item
gates.answer: only items with a signal; a process that is no claude one has null session and item

notes: Plan 2026-10-18: bl_procs reads only a process's command name, never its command line, so headless and interactive are told by the checkout. The planted check names a symlink claude to the interpreter; ps shows it as ./claude on this macOS host (tried 2026-10-18). Data: procs [{pid, age_s, class, checkout, session, item}], worktrees [{path, branch}], stalled [{item, signals}] or absent where the root has no backlog. Layout of the sessions panel (operator's spec): table (pid, age, class, session, item, checkout), an orphan row takes `! `; then `worktrees` (path  branch, joined by ` · `) and `stalled` (a `! ` row: item, then reasons).
